selected_source.summary: The Richfield Flood Risk Prioritization study states that the Richfield stormwater model covers the entire city and the areas of adjacent cities that drain into Richfield. Barr Engineering updated the Richfield PCSWMM model with LiDAR data collected in 2022 and published by the United States Geological Survey. The Richfield model simulates four design storm events that use the Midwest Southeast 3 (MSE3) rainfall distribution. The Richfield study scored flood-risk areas on storm system conditions, critical infrastructure, frequency of flooding, social vulnerability index (SVI), and number of flood-prone structures. The Richfield study evaluated 746 flood-risk areas, with 601 flood-risk areas located within or primarily within the municipal boundary. The City of Richfield selected three flood-risk areas based on the project prioritization framework, and six mitigation concepts were identified and evaluated in the updated stormwater model for those three areas. The Richfield study presents the Section 5 projects, model results, and cost estimates as a concept level design, with all costs presented in 2025 US dollars.

key_excerpts.text: The model covers the entire city and the areas of adjacent cities that drain into Richfield.
Barr updated the existing PCSWMM model to incorporate the Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data collected in 2022 and published by the United States Geological Survey (USGS)
The four design storm events use the Midwest Southeast 3 (MSE3) rainfall distribution

The criteria selected to score the flood-risk areas are:

- Storm system conditions
- Critical infrastructure
- Frequency of flooding
- Social vulnerability index (SVI)
- Number of flood-prone structures
A total of 746 flood-risk areas were evaluated from the study area with 601 flood-risk areas located within or primarily within the municipal boundary.

Three flood-risk areas were selected by the city based on the project prioritization framework developed. For these three flood-risk areas a total of six mitigation concepts were identified and evaluated in the updated stormwater model.
The projects, model results, and cost estimates presented in Section 5 are represent a concept level design.
All costs are presented in 2025 US dollars.
